protocol_step_5_hidden_case.description: Inspected every claim's verdict-assignment code and found that one row (target soo/v003-controlling-pointer-and-part-manifest-repair-20260820) passes a hardcoded literal string 'NOT_SUPPORTED' as its verdict, unlike every other row, which computes verdict via a ternary over the actually observed data (e.g. 'PASS' if paths else 'FAIL'). This is the same class of defect independently found in cohort c7 unit 052 (a verdict field structurally decoupled from the observed evidence it sits next to). Constructed a hidden case: monkey-patched TARGETS for that one claim to point at a commit independently known to contain 93 real pack files (the pinned commit used elsewhere in this same ledger), then re-ran build_ledger() to see whether the verdict would respond to the change in observed data.

protocol_step_5_hidden_case.survival_reasoning: The verdict for this one claim row is not actually computed from the git evidence it is presented alongside; it is a fixed string regardless of what git ls-tree finds. On the real, unmodified pinned commit the producer actually used, the observed matching_path_count happens to be 0 (independently confirmed), so this defect does not currently produce a wrong or invented verdict in the committed ledger -- an empty result and a hardcoded NOT_SUPPORTED are not in tension for that one row. But the mechanism itself does not verify what it claims to verify for that row, and it is not disclosed as a fixed/non-computed field anywhere in the code, the test, or the producer's manifest.json evidence text. This is a real, if narrow, rigor gap: one out of nine ledger rows is not actually evidence-driven, even though its output happens to be truthful by coincidence of the real data. It does not affect the two claims that matter most for the falsifiable hypothesis (the aggregate manifest match and the missing-runtime-file finding), both of which are genuinely computed and were independently reproduced via a wholly separate code path above.
